deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is about the lemniscatic functions written as quotients of entire (theta-type) functions: sl a = P(a)/Q(a) and cl a = p(a)/q(a). Arguments are in degrees, with 180° corresponding to the half-period ϖ, so 60° means ϖ/3. The page itself gives the opening terms of the series: p a = 1 − a²/2 − a⁴/24, q a = 1 + a²/2 − a⁴/24, P a = a − a⁵/60, Q a = 1 + a⁴/12. Check: P/Q = a − a⁵/10 matches sl, and p/q = 1 − a² + a⁴/2 matches cl. The previous page gives log values P(60°) = 0.8654…, Q(60°) = 1.0485961, together with log10 e^{π/18} = 0.0757987. This page derives the closed form behind those numbers.

(1) DUPLICATION. With p, q meaning p(a), q(a): p(2a) = ½p⁴ + p²q² − ½q⁴. Gauss first wrote a bracket ½(...) and then struck the bracket. The correct companion formula is q(2a) = −½p⁴ + p²q² + ½q⁴. Gauss wrote q2 = ½p⁴ − ppqq − ½q⁴, which is the negative of this. The side notes '= −1', '= +1' may be his sign markers.

(2) TRIPLICATION. These are homogeneous forms of degree 9.
- p(3a) = ¼(p⁹ + 6p⁵q⁴ − 3pq⁸).
- q(3a) is only begun ('¾p⁸q'). By a → ia, which swaps p and q, it should be ¼(q⁹ + 6p⁴q⁵ − 3p⁸q) [mine].
- Q(3a) = Q⁹ + 6Q⁵P⁴ − 3QP⁸. A first attempt with P and Q interchanged, P⁹Q + 6P⁴Q⁵ − 3Q⁹, is struck out.
- P(3a) = 3Q⁸P − 6Q⁴P⁵ − P⁹.
Dividing gives the classical lemniscatic triplication sl 3a = s(3 − 6s⁴ − s⁸)/(1 + 6s⁴ − 3s⁸), with s = sl a.

(3) APPLICATION AT 60°. Take a = 60°, so 3a = 180° and P(180°) = 0.
- From P3 = 0, s = sl 60° satisfies 3 − 6x⁴ − x⁸ = 0. Completing the square: x⁸ + 6x⁴ + 9 = 12, so x⁴ = √12 − 3.
- Then Q(180°) = Q(60°)⁹(1 + 6x⁴ − 3x⁸).
- Using x⁸ = 3 − 6x⁴: 1 + 6x⁴ − 3x⁸ = −8 + 24x⁴ = 24√12 − 80 = 8(3√12 − 10).
- So Q60 = [1/(24√12 − 80)]^{1/9} = [(3√12 + 10)/64]^{1/9}, using 1/(3√12 − 10) = (3√12 + 10)/8. The ½·root(1/(3√12 − 10)) line is an intermediate attempt at pulling out 8^{−1/9}.
- The page silently treats Q(180°) as a factor of 1. Numerically [1/(24√12 − 80)]^{1/9} = 0.8807, while the previous page has 1.0485961. The ratio is 1.1907 = e^{π/18}, i.e. Q(180°) = e^{π/2}. That is exactly the log10 e^{π/18} = 0.0757987 term used on the previous page [identification mine].
- The top-left figures (157079… ≈ π/2·10⁵, and the differences 2387, 668) are subsidiary arithmetic.

(4) ADDITION THEOREM.
- The lemniscatic cosine addition formula is cl(a+b) = (cl a cl b − sl a sl b)/(1 + sl a cl a sl b cl b). The page writes it as cos.(a+b) = (cacb − sasb)/(1 + cacbsasb).
- Substituting cl = p/q and sl = P/Q gives cl(a+b) = (pa pb Qa Qb − qa qb Pa Pb)/(qa qb Qa Qb + pa pb Pa Pb).
- Gauss then splits numerator and denominator separately: numerator = p(a+b)·Q(a−b) and denominator = q(a+b)·Q(a−b). The transcription and apparently the ms. read P(a−b) in the numerator. At b = 0 the numerator is pa·Qa, so the factor must be Q(a−b) in both.

(5) SERIES VERIFICATION, lower half of the page.
- He tabulates the four series and partial products, e.g. pa·Pa = a − ½a³ − 7/120 a⁵ (written 'ab − ½a³b − 7/120 a⁵b'), and terms such as −½ab³ and ¼a³b³.
- He also writes a 3×3 product table for (1 + ½a² + a⁴/24)(1 + ½b² + b⁴/24), with entries ¼a²b², 1/48 a⁴b², 1/576 a⁴b⁴, compared against 1 + ½(a+b)² + 1/24 (a+b)⁴. These are low-order checks of the product identity in (4). The table has the sign of a⁴/24 flipped relative to q.
- The next page continues with higher coefficients (1/240, 17/40320, …).

The rest of the page is pen trials: Laplace, Lagrange, Réaumur, Leroi, Loiola, Beurnonville, Gelnhausen, Giebel, Gott, Sünde, geizen, 'ce n'est qu'un vain'.
errors: q2 as written (½p⁴ − ppqq − ½q⁴) equals −q(2a). The correct duplication is q(2a) = −½p⁴ + p²q² + ½q⁴. This is a sign slip, possibly flagged by the '= +1' / '= −1' marginal notes.
q3 = ¾p⁸q is left incomplete. The full form should be ¼(q⁹ + 6p⁴q⁵ − 3p⁸q).

In the product formula, the numerator factor is read as P(a−b). It must be Q(a−b), the same as in the denominator: at b = 0 the numerator equals pa·Qa, not pa·Pa. This is either a slip or a misreading.
Q60 = [1/(1 + 6s⁴ − 3s⁸)]^{1/9} omits the factor Q(180°)^{1/9} = e^{π/18}. This is supplied on the previous page via log 0.0757987, so it is a notational omission, not a real error.
The product table uses +a⁴/24 where q has −a⁴/24. It is probably exploratory.

results.what: Lemniscatic addition theorem cl(a+b) = (cl a cl b − sl a sl b)/(1 + sl a cl a sl b cl b)
results.modern_name: addition theorem for the lemniscatic functions

results.what: Representation sl = P/Q, cl = p/q by entire functions, and the bilinear product formulas p(a+b)Q(a−b) = pa pb Qa Qb − qa qb Pa Pb, q(a+b)Q(a−b) = qa qb Qa Qb + pa pb Pa Pb
results.modern_name: theta-function addition formulas (products θ(a+b)θ(a−b)) in the lemniscatic case
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1829, Fundamenta Nova / theta addition formulas); Gauss's priority is known from his Nachlass (Werke III, X)

results.what: Duplication and triplication of p, q, P, Q as homogeneous forms of degree 4 and 9, e.g. P(3a) = 3Q⁸P − 6Q⁴P⁵ − P⁹ and Q(3a) = Q⁹ + 6Q⁵P⁴ − 3QP⁸
results.modern_name: multiplication formulas for theta functions (lemniscatic case)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi/Abel era; Gauss's lemniscatic versions are in his Nachlass (c. 1798–1800)

results.modern_name: trisection of the lemniscate / special value of sl
special value of a lemniscatic theta function
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (lemniscate Nachlass); in general, theta-function special values

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's theory of the lemniscatic functions via the entire functions P, Q, p, q, with their addition, multiplication and numerical values, is well documented from his Nachlass (Werke III, X; Schlesinger). This page is a working sheet of that known programme. The explicit closed form for Q(60°) is a nice detail, but it is not a new result attributable to anyone later.

transcription_corrections: p2 line: read 'p2 = ½p⁴ + ppqq − ½q⁴'. The opening '½(' is struck through, so this is not ½(p⁴ + ppqq − ½q⁴).
Similarly q2: '½p⁴ − ppqq − ½q⁴', with the struck bracket.
The struck first attempt at Q3 is 'P⁹Q + 6P⁴Q⁵ − 3Q⁹', with P and Q interchanged; the corrected version is 'Q⁹ + 6Q⁵P⁴ − 3QP⁸'.
In the product formula the factor read as 'P(a−b)' on the numerator side must mathematically be Q(a−b); the ms. letter should be rechecked.
Under Q60 the second line '3 − 6 sin60⁴ − sin60⁸' is the vanishing numerator of the triplication (= 0), not part of the radicand.
'1 − ½pa' is probably '1 − ½aa' (the start of the series for p a).
'1 + 1/12 a⁴' and '1 + 1/12 b⁴' (Qa, Qb) are partly over a struck '+'. The '4' beside them is a pen trial.
'sin 60' denotes the lemniscatic sine of 60° (= ϖ/3), not the circular sine.
